content:
Summary

Alright's audience watched iPop Star 2026 but had no reason to return daily or to pay. I designed a daily voting loop where fans back a favourite mentor, win prizes and see their impact on a live leaderboard. An optional membership multiplier lets fans give their mentor extra votes, which tied revenue to something fans already cared about.

heading: My contribution:
content: I framed the problem with product and business leads, set the monetization guardrails (free vote stays free, no pay-to-win feel), designed the end-to-end experience, and ran testing and a staged rollout with data.

Context

Alright is an entertainment app with 5M+ users. iPop Star 2026 was a flagship music show and the company's biggest moment of the year for acquisition. Leadership wanted two outcomes from one feature: grow the app and grow revenue.

cards.heading: Constraints
cards.text: Fixed show calendar, live-night traffic spikes, a short build window and a need to keep the free experience fair.

cards.heading: Stakeholders
cards.text: Product, Engineering, Data, Marketing, the show's content team and Finance.

content:
Problem framing

The brief was "add voting." I reframed it, because voting alone does not create growth or revenue. The real problems were behavioural and commercial.

cards.heading: User
cards.text: Fans watch passively and cannot show support for their favourite mentor.

cards.heading: Behaviour
cards.text: No daily trigger, so viewers leave after each episode.

cards.heading: Business
cards.text: Low upgrade intent. Membership offered no value tied to the show.

heading: How might we
content: Make supporting a mentor a daily habit, and make upgrading feel like a natural way to support them more?

My role and ownership

  • Led design across voting, leaderboard, rewards and membership, working with one other designer on UI.
  • Shaped the roadmap with the PM: what ships for the first live episode and what follows.
  • Set monetization principles and aligned Finance, Marketing and Engineering on them.
  • Defined success metrics and the experiment plan with Data.
  • Handed off specs, states and components to Engineering, and stayed in QA through launch.
